summary: Iteration 3 validation of the two pre-deploy changes: (1) Predictions lock 1 HOUR before kickoff and (2) Leaderboard is real-time with only real users. Added 4 new lock-rule edge tests (2h ahead -> accepted; 30min ahead -> rejected; 59min ahead -> rejected; past -> rejected) using deterministic temporary mutation of match #103's kickoff. Added a Leaderboard cleanliness test (snapshot at session start) verifying exactly 2 real users (Admin + ManchesterUnited76) and no TEST_/Scorer/Aw/Dup/Reg User residue. All 36 backend pytest tests PASS (100%). UI verified: /leaderboard shows 'Standings · Live', green pulsing dot, 'Auto-refresh every 15s', and request listener observed 4 GET /api/leaderboard calls in 32s (initial + 2 polling ticks at ~15s intervals). /fixtures correctly renders 'Locked' badge with padlock and hides Predict button for any match whose kickoff-1h has already passed (visually confirmed on Match #2 which kicked off at 00:00 UTC, and on the dynamically-mutated 30-min-away scratch match). DB returned to pristine state after run (2 users, 0 predictions, 0 awards, match #50/#103/#104 results & times restored).
critical_code_review_comments: submit_prediction (server.py:265) silently swallows ValueError/KeyError when parsing match['time'] - if a future bad data row sneaks in, the predict endpoint will happily save with NO lock check. Recommend logging and returning 500 rather than 'pass'.

Fixtures.jsx parses kickoff with new Date(m.time) where m.time is 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (no 'Z' suffix). Safari/iOS treats this as LOCAL time while Chrome treats it as invalid or local. This means lockAt comparison may be off by the user's timezone offset (e.g., a user in UTC+5:30 might see a match unlocked when the backend has locked it, or vice versa). The backend parses via datetime.fromisoformat then forces tzinfo=UTC, so server & client interpret the same string differently. Recommend the API serve ISO-8601 with explicit 'Z' (e.g., '2026-06-11T15:00:00Z') and the frontend parse accordingly.
Leaderboard.jsx polling has no document.visibilityState guard - it keeps making requests in background tabs. Minor; consider pausing the interval when document.hidden === true.
